newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EXPORTERS FEAR MAY LOSE COMPETITIVENESS IN EMU.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EXPORTERS FEAR MAY LOSE COMPETITIVENESS IN EMU.

text.p: The biggest Finnish exporters fear they may lose competitiveness if Finland joins Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), a study released on Wednesday said.
The study was based on interviews with finance managers of 12 big industrial companies which stood for 38 percent of Finlands' exports in 1995.
The risk of lost competitiveness may increase significantly if Finland joins EMU, said Antti Hakkarainen, researcher at the research institute of the Finnish economy (ETLA) which published the study.

"If the Euro becomes a strong currency, it may cause problems", Hakkarainen said told a news conference, noting that a strong euro could hit Finnish companies' competitiveness particularly in the US and the Far East.
"Some of those interviewed said that if euro area will be founded as planned, they must start production in the US due to the dollar risk", he said.
Hakkarainen said the exporters were particulalrly worried about the possibility that Finland would join EMU while Sweden would stay outside.
"Eighty percent of those interviewed said that from Finand's point of view, it is extremely crucial what kind of EMU decision Sweden will make.
